study: v249 runtime center-part sampling and scalp-projected root-density study

rejected.reason: Stratified near-part sampling increased root count but retained the broad center gap and made parallel comb endpoints more obvious.
Closest-root sampling and reduced crossing angle improved seating but still read as two broad procedural sheets beside a wide scalp channel.
The first projected part-root layer included faces whose projection missed the head, producing a detached rectangle, and its 92 fibers read as thick crossed laces.
Invalid faces were removed and fibers were refined, but the layer sat only 0.2 mm above the scalp cap and was largely hidden by depth competition.
The part narrowed, but regular comb spacing and a hard front transition remained visible.
Visual structure improved, but the four-frame audit found one front-card vertex penetrating 1.577 mm at frame 33.

remainingVisualFailures: Left part-root density transition is still locally visible from the top camera.
Top silhouette still reads as broad procedural sheets instead of interleaved macro locks.
Rear flow lacks layered curved macro-lock breakup.
Browser alpha sorting, memory and frame-rate gates have not run.

decision: Keep r409 as the latest runtime technical prototype. Keep r383 as offline authoring truth and website v83 unchanged.
